title: Project HARLTON: overview
summary: A smarter way to make revenue decisions across several hotels, so that today's quick sale never costs the hotel its most valuable guests tomorrow.

title: HARLTON-01: Peak-Hour Energy Cost Reduction
summary: Predict the few hottest hours of the year that set the hotel's electricity bill, and quietly shift equipment use out of those hours to save money.

title: HARLTON-02: Guest Relocation and Revenue Retention
summary: When one hotel is overbooked, move guests to a sister hotel instead of a competitor, so the guest and the money stay in the group.

title: HARLTON-03: Early Arrival and Late Departure Revenue
summary: Predict how many rooms will be ready early, and sell early check-in and late check-out as paid extras instead of giving them away.

title: HARLTON-04: Amenity Day-Pass Yield Management
summary: On quiet days, sell spare waterpark, pool and spa space to day visitors, while always protecting space for hotel guests.

title: HARLTON-05: Event-Based Parking Pricing
summary: Charge more for parking on busy event nights and less on quiet nights, instead of one flat rate all year.

title: HARLTON-06: Event and Exchange-Rate Demand Signals
summary: Add concerts, holidays, the exchange rate and cross-border travel trends to the forecast, so busy dates are spotted and priced early.

title: HARLTON-07: Vacant-Room Energy Setback
summary: Use the booking system to turn down heating and cooling in rooms nobody has booked tonight, with no new sensors needed.

title: HARLTON-08: Water Leak Detection from Meter Data
summary: Check the water meter every night at 3 AM; if water is still flowing, something is leaking, and the system says roughly where.

title: HARLTON-09: Linen and Amenity Loss Control
summary: Count linen and amenities in and out each week to find where items go missing, and fix the cause instead of just buying more.

title: HARLTON-10: Historical Demand Intelligence
summary: Study several years of past bookings to learn exactly when guests book, who they are and what was turned away, so every future rate is set from evidence.

title: HARLTON-11: Year-Round Occupancy and Room Sales Strategy
summary: A plan for every night of the year that prices busy nights correctly and fills quiet nights with the right guests, groups and packages.

title: Project H2: Unified Executive Business Intelligence
summary: Bring the numbers from every hotel system into one place and deliver simple, automatic reports, so nobody has to build them by hand.

title: H2-01: Cross-Property Shift Exchange
summary: When a shift opens, automatically find a qualified, rested employee, first at the same hotel and then at sister hotels, before paying overtime or agency staff.

title: H2-02: Departure Flow Balancing
summary: Spread guest check-outs across the morning with simple offers and messages, so elevators, the front desk and housekeeping are not overwhelmed at 11 AM.

title: H2-03: Room-Ready Notifications and Housekeeping Sequencing
summary: Clean rooms in the order guests actually need them, and text each guest the moment their room is ready.

title: H2-04: Review-to-Maintenance Intelligence
summary: Read guest reviews every day, pick out real problems such as a noisy air conditioner, and turn them into repair tickets before the next guest complains.

title: H2-05: Automated Schedule Builder
summary: Build the weekly staff schedule automatically, then publish the same approved schedule to the staff app, to the familiar Excel sheet and on paper for the staff board.

title: H2-06: Low-Strain Work Zone Assignment
summary: Give each staff member a compact work area with a fair share of heavy tasks, so nobody walks or lifts more than necessary.

title: H2-07: Night Operations and Front Desk Coverage
summary: Staff the overnight hours based on real night-time demand, take routine paperwork off the night desk and keep staff who work alone safe.

title: H2-08: Security Coverage Optimization
summary: Send security officers where and when problems actually happen, on patrol routes that change every night so they cannot be predicted.

title: H2-09: Centralized Supply Sign-Out and Department Accountability
summary: A simple sign-out sheet, later a tablet, that records who took which supplies, for which department and why, so waste and loss can be traced and reduced.

title: H2-10: Decentralized Supply and Amenity Placement
summary: Keep supplies close to where they are used, in hotels and restaurants alike, so staff spend less time walking to the storeroom.

title: Data Foundation
summary: One agreed set of tables, labels and rules that every report uses, so the same question always gets the same, trustworthy answer.

title: Further Ideas: Potential and Limitations
summary: Promising ideas that are not ready yet, each listed honestly with what is missing and what would make it work.
